items.title: Cyber incident disrupting services for Pacific Blue Cross members
items.author: Dissent
items.content: <article>CBC reports: Pacific Blue Cross says it’s dealing with a “cyber incident” that has disrupted some of its systems, leaving members unable to access certain services, including its website and contact centre. The Burnaby-based health benefits provider, which serves approximately 1.7 million British Columbians, says it first became aware of the disruption early Wednesday, Nov....</article>

items.title: Department of Health Care Access and Information (HCAI) notifies individuals of data security incident discovered in May.
items.author: Dissent
items.content: <article>On November 16, California’s Department of Health Care Access and Information (HCAI) mailed notification letters to individuals affected by an incident they discovered on May 27, 2026: On May 27, 2026, HCAI discovered that some grant, scholarship, and loan applications submitted through our Funding Portal 1.0 could be accessed by certain search engine links. This...</article>

items.title: The Biggest Data Breach Settlements of 2026
items.author: Dissent
items.content: <article>James Coker writes: In 2026, we saw a vast number of class action settlement agreements reached in regard to high-profile data breach incidents that have taken place during the past few years, some of which have also been subject to separate regulatory action. Here are the biggest data breach class action settlement agreements announced in...</article>

items.title: Hackers breach US Air Force Cloud One platform, putting military data at risk
items.author: Dissent
items.content: <article>Reuters reports: Hackers have breached the US Air Force’s flagship cloud computing platform, three people familiar with the matter said, in a development that could jeopardise a vast swathe of sensitive tactical, personnel and logistics data. The intrusion at Cloud One was discovered within the past month or so during work to upgrade the system,...</article>

items.title: Barclays’ US banking arm confirms data breach
items.author: Dissent
items.content: <article>Paulina Okunytė reports: The American branch of British multinational bank Barclays has suffered a data breach, exposing credit card application data. Barclays Bank Delaware, a US banking subsidiary that issues credit cards to American consumers, has started informing affected customers. According to a breach notice sent to affected individuals and shared with the authorities, an...</article>

items.title: Global news agency AFP reports cyberattack, shuts down content platform
items.author: Dissent
items.content: <article>Al Jazeera Staff and AFP report: Agence France-Presse (AFP) has been hit by a cyberattack, requiring the AFP Forum content platform to be taken offline. The France-based international news agency’s management said on Thursday that it is currently investigating the circumstances of the cyberattack, including who was behind it. “AFP was hit by a cyber...</article>

items.title: Korea Scientists and Engineers Mutual-aid Association Hit by Hack, 210,000 Records Leaked
items.author: Dissent
items.content: <article>Lee Young-ho reports: According to industry sources on the 27th, the association detected the cyber breach early this month and commissioned a detailed investigation by an outside specialist agency. The probe confirmed on the 25th that about 210,000 pieces of member information had been leaked, including membership numbers, 13 types of internal identification codes, member...</article>

items.title: Happy Thanksgiving!
items.author: Dissent
items.content: <article>Regular news updates will resume tonight. In the meantime, thank you to all who read this site or who send me tips and helpful information. This is DataBreaches.net’s 17th Thanksgiving, and attempts to censor news or opinions have never been more concerning. Those of you who support journalists—whether by donations, kind words, or encouragement to...</article>

items.title: FIFA says it has been victim of a cyberattack accessing ‘personal and business information’
items.author: Dissent
items.content: <article>CNA reports:  FIFA was the victim of a cyberattack that saw hackers gain access to what soccer’s world governing body describes as a “limited set of personal and business information,” it said on Thursday (Nov 26). “FIFA is working closely with the relevant authorities, including law enforcement,” the organisation said in a statement sent to...</article>

items.title: Preinstalled Keenadu malware turns up on 220,000+ Android devices
items.author: Dissent
items.content: <article>Sinisa Markovic reports: A new Android phone can come out of the box with malware already in its firmware, and the number of such devices detected each month has grown more than 2.5 times over the past year, according to Kaspersky. Keenadu, one of the two families behind most of these infections, landed on more...</article>

items.title: Australia’s Flight Centre Data Breach Exposes Customer Records and Passport Details
items.author: Dissent
items.content: <article>Pierluigi Paganini reports: Australia’s Flight Centre Travel Group is investigating a cyber incident involving a third-party accommodation booking system that may have exposed a significant number of customer records. The company disclosed the incident on November 26, saying it had detected unusual activity in a platform used by several of its leisure travel brands. The...</article>

items.title: 1Password says a hacker used an employee’s GitHub account to take customer data
items.author: Dissent
items.content: <article>Dave Barr reports: Malicious code sent through one employee’s corporate GitHub account made 1Password’s own backend services download customer records, the company said in an incident post on Wednesday, November 25. The intruder also copied source code from private repositories and got into the CI/CD system, the pipeline that builds and ships software. 1Password started...</article>

items.title: ‘We are not ShinyHunters,’ says criminal hacking crew that looks and acts just like ShinyHunters
items.author: Dissent
items.content: <article>So if it looks like a duck, walks like a duck, and vishes like a duck, it’s still not a duck.  Jessica Lyons reports: Inception, a new data theft and extortion gang that security researchers have theorized is a rebrand of the ShinyHunters group, “reject[s] this attribution” and claims it has no affiliation with any...</article>

items.title: Treasury’s FinCEN says ‘cybersecurity incident’ includes ‘unauthorized access’ of some systems
items.author: Dissent
items.content: <article>ABC News reports: The Treasury Department’s Financial Crimes Enforcement Network (FinCEN) is “investigating a cybersecurity incident that resulted in unauthorized access to a limited subset of its systems,” and has taken some systems offline as a precaution, according to an alert posted on its site. The agency handles sensitive information and reports about financial crimes...</article>
